metricText: Women as a percentage of filled seats in Ghana's single parliamentary chamber for a fixed IPU monthly-ranking snapshot.
note: PROPOSED: The official IPU August 2026 ranking prints 276 filled seats, 40 women, and 14.5% women for Ghana, but admission requires a reviewed ipu-parline parser, a fixed annual snapshot rule with election-linked resolution, and authenticated first-print custody. Act 1121's First Schedule ends at 2034, despite a conflicting 2030 statement in an official Parliament transcript. The all-seat IPU share is an accountability context series, not by itself Act 1121's statutory compliance denominator. gh-act-1121-affirmative-action is a reserved future bills/ slug; no such entry exists yet.
statisticalProduct: IPU Parline, Monthly ranking of women in national parliaments

verification.reason: The official IPU ranking API returns one unambiguous Ghana lower-or-single-chamber row for the requested month, but this is a new adapter family and one current fetch does not authenticate an annual or election-linked first print. The captured Act scan also shows that overall elected-seat share is contextual rather than the direct denominator named by sections 18 and 20.

artifact.reportTitle: Monthly ranking of women in national parliaments

statutoryAnchor.sourceClassification: Primary enacted statutory text in a scan hosted by the secondary FAOLEX legal repository; not a Ghana-government origin URL.
statutoryAnchor.title: Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121)

section18.relationship: The First Schedule applies to appointments to Parliament leadership positions and Committees of Parliament.

section20.relationship: The First Schedule applies to participation and representation in party politics, including candidate sponsorship and party officials.

scope.seriesRelationship: IPU's share of all filled parliamentary seats is a related accountability measure, not a direct statutory-compliance denominator stated in these sections.

officialMinistrySummary.sourceClassification: Official Ghana Ministry communication summarizing the Act; not the enacted instrument.
officialMinistrySummary.printedScheduleExcerpt: 30 per cent women representation in decision-making from 2024 to 2026, 35 per cent from 2027 to 2028, and 50 per cent by 2034

publicSourceDiscrepancy.resolution: The captured enacted-text scan and official Ministry summary say 2034. The following official Parliament transcript preserves a member's conflicting 2030 statement but is not the enacted legal text.

conflictingArtifact.sourceClassification: Official Parliament transcript of a member's statement; not enacted-law text.
conflictingArtifact.speaker: Hon Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah
conflictingArtifact.printedExcerpt: from 30 per cent in 2026 to 50 per cent by the year 2030

firstPrint.blocker: A post-release fetch of a requested monthly ranking does not prove the first IPU response for a registered annual or election-linked snapshot, preserve later corrections, or establish reviewed capture custody.

requiredWork: Implement and review an ipu-parline parser that selects country_code GH, requires lower_data_missing false, and extracts filled seats, women, and percent women from one fixed monthly-ranking response.
Define the annual snapshot month and election-linked resolution rule, then add release-time witnessed or versioned custody and genuine historical pins before admission.
Keep the IPU all-seat share labeled as an accountability context series rather than a direct Act 1121 compliance denominator.
parseNotes: Use the lower-or-single-chamber fields; Ghana has no upper-chamber values in the captured row.
Preserve IPU's printed one-decimal percentage and cross-check it against 100 times women divided by filled seats, allowing only the displayed rounding.

The underlying representation changes irregularly and is election-driven; operational registration should use an annual observation with an election-linked resolution rather than claiming a naturally annual source cadence.
